newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails former securities firm president.
newsitem.headline: China jails former securities firm president.

text.p: A Chinese court has sentenced the former head of one of Shanghai's biggest securities firms to 17 years in prison for embezzlement and taking bribes, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
Guan Jinsheng was removed from his post at the Shanghai International Securities Company after a huge scandal involving treasury bill futures that rocked the Shanghai exchange in February 1995.
The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate Court convicted Guan of accepting 294,000 yuan ($35,000) in bribes and misappropriating 2.4 million yuan in public funds between 1992 and 1994, Xinhua said.

Guan, who was seen as the godfather of Shanghai's securities industry before his fall from grace, disappeared from public view after his removal following the February scandal, which prompted China to later ban all bond futures trading.
Shanghai International, which suffered heavy losses after taking a position far exceeding its legal maximum, was later merged with the former Shanghai Shenyin Securities.
Guan had also previously held the posts of president of the Shanghai Wanguo Real Estate Development Corp and board chairman of the Shanghai Wanguo (Hong Kong) Co, Xinhua said but gave no details.
